substeps.caption: No door or guard: a flat sample (here a 40 mm square cut from a print; 3 x 3 x 1.5 mm at the least) goes on the platen by hand, unclamped.
Hands clear: the indenter comes down out of its cylinder and presses the 1 mm-radius ball in, an indent 0.25-1 mm wide. The profilometer waits at the right, clear of the platen.
The indenter lifts well clear; the profilometer's carriage runs in along the crosshead and its pick-up passes under the indenter to the indent.
The stylus traces across the indent, line by line, to map its 3D shape.
It lifts and runs back out to the right, and the indenter goes back to its start.
CORSICA fits a stress-strain curve to that profile in minutes. The sample comes off.
